blocks.title: Heat engine
blocks.text: A heat engine converts some thermal energy to mechanical work. Usually the heat comes from the burning of a fuel. The earliest heat engine was the steam engine, developed on the fact that when water is boiled in a vessel covered with a lid, the steam inside tries to push the lid off, showing the ability to do work; this observation helped to develop a steam engine. The steam engine is a thermodynamical system (Do You Know).

The working principle of a heat engine is based on the conversion of heat energy into mechanical work through a cyclic process. It involves the cyclic transfer of heat energy from a high-temperature reservoir to a low-temperature reservoir, with the objective of converting as much heat as possible into mechanical work. This process is governed by thermodynamic principles and is essential in various applications where mechanical energy is required from heat sources.

blocks.caption: The heat engine in outline
rows: the working substance absorbs heat from a hot reservoir (burning fuel)
part of the heat becomes mechanical work
the rest is rejected to a cold reservoir
the working substance returns to its initial state and repeats

blocks.prompt: Why must a heat engine work in a cycle, and where does the heat that is not turned into work go?
blocks.explanation: Only a cyclic process lets the engine deliver work continuously, returning the working substance to its starting state each time so that its internal energy change over a cycle is zero. The heat not converted into work is expelled to the low-temperature reservoir, the surroundings.

items: Heat engine: converts thermal energy (usually from burning fuel) into mechanical work by a cyclic transfer of heat from a hot reservoir to a cold reservoir; the steam engine was the first.
